summary: GCP folder-level IAM Deny policy preventing service-account impersonation for preprod/staging CI workflows
description:
Issue summary: Several CI pipelines targeting preprod/staging began failing with permission denied errors when attempting to impersonate deployment service accounts. Impact: deployment and smoke tests for feature branches are blocked; engineers cannot provision new preprod test clusters. Timeline: failures started ~2026-03-10 09:40 UTC after folder-level security hardening changes rolled by SecOps.

Primary failure mode: Service account token requests return 403 with: 'Request had insufficient authentication scopes' and 'Permission denied by organizational Deny policy'.

Why this matters: Preprod/staging runs are a gating step for Dedicated/Private customer rollouts. This access break prevents releases and blocks several active feature rollouts.
impact: CI pipelines failing across ~12 pipelines; estimated 8 engineering teams blocked; release window at risk for next maintenance window.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger preprod deployment job that impersonates svc-deployer-staging service account
Job attempts to call IAMCredentials:generateAccessToken and fails with 403
Review IAM audit logs for request and observe 'denied by policy' entries referencing organizations/67890/policies/deny-llm-privilege-elevations
investigation_notes: Observed a folder-level 'deny' policy applied at folders/987654 which blocks iamcredentials.generateAccessToken for serviceAccount impersonation unless an allow-exception exists.
Change was rolled by SecOps (see Slack thread #secops-policy and PR) as part of hardening sprint; it unintentionally scoped down impersonation for two CI service accounts.
Reproduced error locally by calling iamcredentials.generateAccessToken using gcloud with --impersonate-service-account and observed same 403 and Deny policy reference.
Checked Cloud Asset inventory: deny policy id deny-llm-privilege-elevations created 2026-03-10T09:30 by user: liam.kaufman@redwood.com (SecOps).
Cross-checked with INT-30421 (scoped-readonly-cloud-trace-access) for recent related permission changes; potential overlap in policy targeting tags/labels.
mitigation_attempted: Requested temporary exception from SecOps to allow iamcredentials.generateAccessToken for affected service accounts (approved in principle, pending policy change)
As a short-term workaround, CI jobs were reconfigured to use long-lived deploy tokens (reduced security posture) for a subset of non-sensitive pipelines to unblock high-priority releases
Added a conservative retry wrapper to deployment task to surface clearer errors to engineers while fix is in progress
resolution_plan: Coordinate with SecOps to add explicit allow-exception in folder deny policy for two CI service accounts and CI runner instances within a specific resource name scope
Create an automated audit that surfaces any future deny-policy rollouts that would target serviceAccount impersonation and notify #infra and #secops before enforcement
Document runbook for emergency breakglass steps for CI impersonation failures and add to Confluence page
Replace long-lived deploy tokens with short-lived token broker flow after policy change to restore secure posture

next_steps: Coordinate maintenance window and verify CI pipelines post-change
Follow up with a postmortem and update Confluence runbook within 72 hours
